land.text: the Erivan Governorate, where the Armenian National Council 'declared Armenia's independence' on 28 May 1918 after the Transcaucasian federation fell

predecessors.note: No dossier or Cliopatria row exists for the federation (1918); it also precedes the Azerbaijani and Georgian republics.

land.text: the republic 'Sovietised' on 2 December 1920; 'most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia' (war page)

successors.note: Soviet power was proclaimed by the Revkom on 29 November 1920 and the government handed over on 2 December.

land.text: Zangezur, listed in the infobox as a successor 'Republic of Mountainous Armenia'

successors.note: Named in the infobox only; no dossier exists. The Armenia-Azerbaijan war page says Zangezur was 'ceded by Azerbaijan to Armenia in November 1920'.

land.text: the Kars region: the city occupied on 30 October 1920, ceded by the Treaty of Alexandropol of 3 December 1920

successors.note: The infobox lists 'Turkey' as successor; the Republic of Turkey is 1923/24 and Cliopatria has no row for the Ankara government of 1920, so this is the closest slug.

capitals.name: Yerevan
capitals.note: Infobox: Capital Yerevan; the page does not list Alexandropol as a capital.

keyframe_review.note: 16,537 km2 against the infobox's 11,396 km2 'after the Treaty of Batum' (4 June 1918; the text says 13,000 km2): a ratio of 1.45. The Ottoman evacuation in November 1918 added '6,000 square miles (16,000 square kilometres)', so the 1918 year runs from about 11-13,000 to about 27-29,000 km2 and the single Cliopatria shape sits between the two; within a factor of two, kept. The ledger carries the November gain.

40,911 km2 against 'more than 17,000 square miles (44,000 square kilometres)' after Kars was annexed in spring 1919: a ratio of 0.93. The shape reaches 42.99 E (Kars) and 38.87 N. It cannot show the year's changes: the Armenian capture of Nakhichevan city in June 1919 and its loss in July, and Azerbaijan's Zangezur offensive of 3 November 1919, which was beaten off.

correction.text: the 1919 shape carried into 1920 as the republic's extent at the start of the year; the Turkish invasion of 28 September took the city of Kars on 30 October (ledger loss) and the Treaty of Alexandropol (3 December 1920) confined Armenia 'to the province of Yerevan, thereby ceding Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu', leaving '27,000-30,044 km2' (infobox); draw the shape minus Kars from October

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria stops in 1919 but the republic lasted to 2 December 1920. The infobox gives 27,000-30,044 km2 'after the Treaty of Alexandropol' against the carried 1919 shape's 40,911 km2 (0.66-0.73) and 45,325 km2 for 1919 (0.90 against the shape). The page does give the date and the places of the loss: the Turkish army 'occupied the city of Kars' on 30 October 1920 and the treaty of 3 December ceded Kars, Nakhchivan and Surmalu (the ledger's Kars loss and the treaty's contest_end). It does not give districts or areas for these, and the gazetteer shows that the shape holds only about 2,000 km2 of Kars province (8 cells) and nothing of Iğdır (Surmalu), so Kars explains little of the gap in area: the 1919 shape probably under-reaches in the west and over-reaches at Nakhichevan, which the page has under Soviet Azerbaijan by the end of 1920. The shape is kept as the best available; the rendering agent draws it minus Kars from October 1920.

region.text: the Erivan Governorate, where 'the Armenian National Council declared Armenia's independence' (28 May 1918)

ledger.note: 28 May 1918: the Armenian National Council declares Armenia's independence. Infobox 'Declaration of Independence: 28 May 1918'; 'from May (28th de jure, 30th de facto)'. The page names the Erivan Governorate as what the Ottomans later evacuated, not as the founding territory.

region.text: the Erivan Governorate, where the Ottomans 'resumed their offensive in Armenia on 21 May' and were beaten at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad

ledger.note: 21 May 1918: the Ottoman offensive in Armenia; at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad 'local Armenian forces emerged victorious'.
4 June 1918: the Treaty of Batum ends the fighting and leaves Armenia 11,396 km2 (infobox; 13,000 km2 in the text). 'The Treaty of Batum was thereafter signed on 4 June.'

region.text: the Erivan Governorate: 'Ottoman forces evacuated the Erivan Governorate' and Armenia gained '6,000 square miles (16,000 square kilometres)'

ledger.note: November 1918: after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) the Ottoman army leaves the Erivan Governorate and Armenia grows by about 16,000 km2.

region.text: Karabakh (the advance towards Shusha) and Zangezur, the base of Andranik's advance

ledger.note: Late November 1918: Andranik's offensive into Karabakh. Andranik page: 'By the end of October, Andranik's Special Striking Division concentrated on the border between Zangezur and Karabakh'; 'the offensive commenced in late November' towards Shusha; 'By early December, Andranik was within 40 km (25 miles) of Shusha'; on British assurances he halted and 'In December 1918' withdrew from Karabakh to Goris. The Armenian-Azerbaijani war page says only that 'Armenian forces under Andranik seized Nagorno-Karabakh' after Mudros, with no date; the month is the Andranik page's, the zone (Karabakh and Zangezur) my reading, so confidence 2 (was 1). The page does not say he held Shusha or any town, so the contest is of ground taken or threatened, not of a held line.

region.text: the Armenian-Georgian frontier, fought over in the Armeno-Georgian War

ledger.note: 7 December 1918: Armenian-Georgian skirmishes begin ('Skirmishes began on 7 December'). The page names no district; the frontier band is my reading.
31 December 1918: the ceasefire takes effect 'at midnight on 31 December'.

region.text: the Kars Oblast: 'In the spring of 1919, Armenia, with British support, incorporated the formerly occupied regions of Kars and Nakhchivan', bringing Armenia to 'more than 17,000 square miles (44,000 square kilometres)'

ledger.note: April 1919: Armenia takes over Kars. 'The Southwest Caucasus Republic administered the entire Kars and Batum oblasts', 'leading to its capitulation by Armenian and British forces on 10 April 1919.' Reviewer eu-19-f: counterpart was 'nobody' (the note said the page does not name Kars's holder; it does) and month 4 added; the Southwest Caucasian Republic has no dossier yet. The ottoman-empire dossier dates the British occupation of Kars to 19 April 1919.

region.text: Nakhichevan: 'Armenia's annexation of Nakhchivan was announced on 3 May 1919'; 'They managed to capture the city of Nakhichevan in June 1919'

ledger.note: June 1919: Drastamat Kanayan's Armenian troops take Nakhichevan city and destroy the Republic of Aras; Azerbaijani and Ottoman troops retook it in July.
10 August 1919: ceasefire over Nakhichevan ('On 10 August 1919, a ceasefire was signed'); the dispute itself went on to 1920, so this ends only the 1919 fighting.

28 April 1920: the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic ceases to exist when the Soviet 11th Army occupies it; the Armenian claim passes to Soviet Azerbaijan. By the end of April 'Armenian forces controlled most of western Azerbaijan, including Karabakh and Nakhichevan' (war page).

region.text: Karabakh, Nakhichevan and Zangezur, contested with Soviet Azerbaijan

ledger.note: April-May 1920: the Soviet 11th Army 'conquered Karabakh in May 1920'; Nakhichevan 'was Sovietized later in 1920'.

region.text: the Kars front, where Turkey 'invaded Armenia on 28 September 1920'

ledger.note: 28 September 1920: the Turkish army under Karabekir invades Armenia.

region.text: 'On 30 October, the Turkish army occupied the city of Kars'

ledger.note: 30 October 1920: in the invasion begun on 28 September the Turkish army under Karabekir occupies the city of Kars, 'supposed to be impregnable', leaving its 25,000 defenders disorganised (page). The Treaty of Alexandropol of 3 December 1920 then cedes Kars (see the contest_end below). The page names the city; the region is the modern Kars province, my reading, and only about 2,000 km2 of it (8 of 159 cells, by the gazetteer) lies inside Cliopatria's 1919 shape. Counterpart: the Ankara government of the Turkish National Movement, for which no dossier exists yet.

November 1920: Zangezur 'ceded by Azerbaijan to Armenia' as a 'symbol of friendship'; the war ends (infobox 28 November 1920). Karabakh and Nakhichevan stay with Soviet Azerbaijan (Treaty of Moscow, 16 March 1921, for Nakhichevan).

3 December 1920: Karabekir 'imposed on Armenia the Treaty of Alexandropol'; Armenia 'was confined to the province of Yerevan, thereby ceding Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu' (page). The area after it is 27,000-30,044 km2 (infobox). The Kars loss is dated above (30 October); the page gives no event for the Surmalu and Nakhchivan cessions: Surmalu (modern Igdir) has no cells in Cliopatria's 1919 shape, and Nakhichevan was in Soviet Azerbaijan's hands (see the contest above).

region.text: the republic Sovietised on 2 December 1920, without the Kars land that the Turkish army occupied on 30 October 1920

ledger.note: 2 December 1920: 'due to the threat of a Soviet ultimatum' the government hands power to the Soviets; the Revkom had proclaimed Soviet rule on 29 November. The Treaty of Alexandropol was imposed the next day. The land that passes to the Armenian SSR is the 1919 shape without Kars (lost to the Turkish army on 30 October). Nakhichevan and the Karabakh edge of the shape are still inside it: the pages leave their exact hand-over to Soviet Azerbaijan undated, see notes.

wars.name: Battle of Sardarabad and the Ottoman offensive of May 1918
wars.outcome: Armenian forces won at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad; the Treaty of Batum of 4 June 1918 left Armenia 11,396 km2.
wars.note: The Ottomans evacuated the Erivan Governorate only after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918).

wars.name: Armeno-Georgian War
wars.outcome: Skirmishes from 7 December 1918 and a ceasefire from midnight on 31 December; the page opened gives no change of frontier.
wars.note: The disputed districts are not named on the page opened.

wars.name: Armenian-Azerbaijani war (1918-1920)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive (infobox, 30 March 1918 - 28 November 1920): 'Most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia'; the Karabakh and Nakhichevan disputes settled for Soviet Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan's attack on Zangezur on 3 November 1919 was beaten off; Nakhichevan city changed hands in June and July 1919.
wars.note: The Wikipedia article is 'Armenian-Azerbaijani war (1918-1920)'. The war page gives no date for Andranik's seizure of Karabakh (the Andranik page dates his offensive to late November 1918) nor for the British appointment of Sultanov as governor-general of Karabakh and Zangezur.

wars.name: Turkish-Armenian War
wars.outcome: Turkey invaded on 28 September 1920, occupied the city of Kars on 30 October and imposed the Treaty of Alexandropol on 3 December 1920, ceding 'Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu' and leaving Armenia 27,000-30,044 km2.
wars.note: The page names the cession (Kars, Nakhchivan, Surmalu) and the 30 October occupation of Kars; it gives no battle other than the invasion, and no district boundaries.

certainty.note: Most frontiers were contested or occupied (Karabakh, Zangezur, Nakhichevan, Kars, the Georgian border); only the Batum line of 4 June 1918 and the Alexandropol line of 3 December 1920 were treaty lines, and the page does not describe them.

notes:
Armenia and Republic of Armenia: Cliopatria's two rows share Wikidata Q399 and Wikipedia title 'Armenia', but they are different states: the First Republic of Armenia (28 May 1918 - 2 December 1920, this dossier) and the Republic of Armenia declared in 1991 and drawn by Cliopatria from 1992 (slug republic-of-armenia, another agent), with the Armenian SSR (armenian-soviet-socialist-republic) between. They are not merged here. The Wikipedia field is set to 'First Republic of Armenia' (accurate for 1918-1920) although Cliopatria's is 'Armenia'.
Scope: Cliopatria ends the state in 1919; the infobox dissolves it on 2 December 1920. A one-year keyframe for 1920 (the 1919 shape) extends it.
Open points: the territory of 1918 inside the Erivan Governorate before and after Mudros; which land Alexandropol took (the page gives areas, not districts); the Karabakh and Zangezur sequence (Andranik, Sultanov, the 22 August 1919 agreement, which the war page does not mention, though the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic page frames Karabakh as disputed). The Treaty of Sevres (10 August 1920) is not drawn: the page cites 103,599 km2 for the treaty; the Treaty of Kars is not on the page. Page budget (2 of 2) spent.
Counterparts needing a dossier: transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic (1918); republic-of-mountainous-armenia (1921); grand-national-assembly-of-turkey (the Ankara government, 1920; counterpart of the Kars loss of 30 October 1920 and of the Turkish-Armenian war; republic-of-turkey starts only in 1923); (the Georgian republic is the `georgia` dossier, 1918-2024, which carries the mirror contest pair; southwest-caucasian-republic, 1918-1919, is the counterpart of the April 1919 Kars gain and has no dossier). Repair pass 2026-11-01: added the loss of Kars (30 October 1920, counterpart grand-national-assembly-of-turkey) and took Kars out of the dissolve region; corrected the 1920 keyframe, the Alexandropol contest_end and the Turkish-Armenian war note, which wrongly said the page gives no date or place for the loss; replaced the counterpart name 'Turkish National Movement' by the slug in the two contest events and the war; dated Andranik's Karabakh offensive to late November 1918 from the Andranik page (confidence 2). Still open: the Surmalu and Nakhchivan cessions of Alexandropol have no event of their own (Surmalu is outside the Cliopatria 1919 shape; Nakhichevan's hand-over to Soviet Azerbaijan is undated on the pages opened), so the dissolve region still contains Nakhichevan.
